summary: The Restaurant class holds one method that turns a numeric spice rating into a human-readable label, using a switch expression to map each valid number 1 through 5 to its own description and catching anything else with a default answer.

lines.text: Declares the class that groups the restaurant's behaviour; the file must be named Restaurant.java to match.
The method takes the numeric rating as an int and hands back a String, so the caller supplies a number and receives wording it can display.
This is a switch expression rather than a switch statement: the whole switch produces a single value, and that value is what gets returned.
The arrow form pairs one input with one result and does not fall through to the next case, so no break keyword is needed.
Rounds out the five documented levels, giving the hottest rating its label.
Every switch expression must produce a value for any possible input, so this branch covers 0, 6, negatives, and anything else outside the 1-5 range.
